summary: LLM API costs can spiral quickly at scale — a customer support bot handling 1M conversations monthly can cost $3,250+ with flagship models, but a layered optimization strategy combining caching, model routing, and prompt engineering can cut that spend by 60–95%. Research from PwC in January 2026 found prompt caching alone reduces API costs by 41–80% across OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, while semantic caching adds another layer by eliminating entire redundant requests. Combining techniques like prompt compression (30% token reduction), semantic caching (45% cache hit rate), model routing, and batch APIs, teams have demonstrated up to 80% total cost reduction within a 6-week implementation window.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching (Provider-Native)
techniques.description: Stores computed key-value tensors for repeated prompt prefixes server-side, so the model skips reprocessing static content on subsequent requests. Every major provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google) now ships this natively. The static portion of your prompt — system instructions, knowledge base, few-shot examples — must appear at the beginning and remain unchanged across calls.
techniques.savings: Up to 90% reduction on cached input token costs; 41–80% overall API cost reduction; 13–31% improvement in time-to-first-token
techniques.example: A RAG pipeline passing a 20,000-token knowledge base on every request moves that context to the top of the system prompt unchanged; Anthropic caches it after the first call and charges 90% less on subsequent cached prefix tokens, requiring zero code changes beyond prompt ordering.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Intercepts incoming queries, converts them to embeddings, and checks a vector store for semantically similar previous queries. If a match is found above a similarity threshold, the cached response is returned without ever hitting the LLM API. Complements provider-native prompt caching by eliminating entire requests rather than just discounting repeated prefixes.
techniques.savings: 45% cache hit rate in production; eliminates 100% of token costs for cache hits
techniques.example: A customer support chatbot using Redis semantic cache stores embeddings of previous Q&A pairs; when a user asks 'How do I reset my password?' after someone already asked 'What are the steps to change my password?', the cached answer is returned instantly at zero API cost.

techniques.name: Model Routing
techniques.description: Classifies incoming requests by complexity and routes them to the cheapest model capable of handling the task. Simple classification, extraction, or FAQ tasks go to budget-tier models; only complex reasoning or nuanced generation tasks escalate to frontier models. A typical production split sends 70% of traffic to cheap models and only 5% to the most expensive.
techniques.savings: 50–70% reduction in average cost per request depending on traffic mix
techniques.example: Using LiteLLM's router, classification and entity extraction tasks route to GPT-3.5 or Haiku 4.5 ($1/$5 per million tokens), while multi-step reasoning routes to Claude Sonnet 4.6 ($3/$15), and only ambiguous escalations hit Opus 4.8 ($5/$25) — achieving a weighted average cost 65% lower than using Opus for everything.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression
techniques.description: Reduces the token count of input prompts by removing redundant phrasing, compressing few-shot examples, trimming verbose instructions, and replacing long format descriptions with structured schemas. Every token removed from input directly reduces cost proportionally. Techniques include using structured output schemas, cutting filler phrases, and limiting system prompts to under 200 tokens.
techniques.example: Replacing a verbose 400-token system prompt that says 'Please respond in a helpful, friendly, and professional manner, formatting your answer as a JSON object with fields for...' with a terse 120-token structured schema instruction cuts input costs by 30% on every single API call with no quality loss.

techniques.name: Output Constraints (max_tokens + Structured Output)
techniques.description: Explicitly setting max_tokens in API calls prevents runaway verbose responses, and using structured output formats (JSON schema, function calling) forces models to return only necessary fields rather than explanatory prose. Output tokens cost 4–5x more than input tokens at flagship model pricing, making this disproportionately impactful.
techniques.savings: Up to 50% reduction in output token usage
techniques.example: Setting max_tokens=150 and specifying a JSON response schema with three fields (intent, confidence, next_action) instead of free-text responses reduces a typical 300-token output to under 80 tokens — saving $10+ per million output tokens at GPT-4 pricing.

techniques.name: Batch API Processing
techniques.description: Groups multiple non-urgent requests and submits them as a batch job rather than real-time API calls. Providers offer significant discounts for batch workloads since they can be processed during off-peak hours. Anthropic's batch API offers 50% off standard pricing. Best suited for offline workflows like data labeling, content generation pipelines, or nightly processing jobs.
techniques.savings: 50% reduction in API costs for eligible workloads
techniques.example: A content team generating 10,000 product descriptions nightly switches from real-time API calls to Anthropic's batch API, halving their Claude Sonnet costs from $0.15 to $0.075 per thousand descriptions with no change in output quality.

techniques.name: Right-Sizing Model Selection
techniques.description: Benchmarking your specific tasks against multiple model tiers to find the cheapest model that meets your quality bar. Many tasks that developers default to using GPT-4 or Claude Opus for can be handled adequately by Haiku, GPT-3.5, or Gemini Flash at 10–20x lower cost. Requires systematic evaluation but delivers permanent per-call savings.
techniques.savings: 60–90% cost reduction if a cheaper model meets quality requirements
techniques.example: Running a 200-prompt eval set through both Claude Haiku 4.5 ($1/$5 per million tokens) and Claude Opus 4.8 ($5/$25) reveals that Haiku achieves 94% of Opus quality on intent classification — dropping the default model saves 80% on that workload immediately.

techniques.name: RAG Optimization and Reranking
techniques.description: Optimizes Retrieval-Augmented Generation pipelines by retrieving fewer, more relevant chunks and using a reranker to select only the highest-quality context before passing it to the LLM. Reduces the number of tokens passed as context on every request. Smaller, denser context windows mean lower input costs and often better model focus.
techniques.savings: 20–40% reduction in input tokens per RAG request
techniques.example: A legal document assistant previously retrieved 15 chunks (6,000 tokens) per query; adding a cross-encoder reranker drops the passed context to the top 5 chunks (2,000 tokens), cutting input costs by 67% on the context portion of every request.

techniques.name: Streaming with Early Termination
techniques.description: Uses streaming responses to detect when the model has produced sufficient output and terminates the connection early, avoiding billing for tokens generated after a logical stopping point is reached. Useful for classification, yes/no answers, or structured fields where the model may continue generating padding text.
techniques.savings: 10–30% reduction in output token usage for applicable tasks
techniques.example: A sentiment classification endpoint streams the response and closes the connection as soon as a valid JSON closing brace is detected, stopping generation at token 40 instead of letting the model reach max_tokens at 200.

techniques.name: Combined Prompt + Batch Caching Stack
techniques.description: Layering provider-native prompt caching with batch API discounts for the highest total reduction. Anthropic's documentation confirms combining both achieves up to 95% cost reduction versus standard real-time calls with full context on every request.
techniques.savings: Up to 95% total cost reduction versus uncached real-time calls
techniques.example: An overnight data enrichment pipeline uses Anthropic batch API (50% off) with a 10,000-token static system prompt that is cached (90% off input tokens), reducing a job that would cost $500 at list price to approximately $25–30 in practice.

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Open-source unified LLM proxy that provides a single OpenAI-compatible API interface to 100+ models. Includes built-in model routing, fallbacks, load balancing, cost tracking, and semantic caching. Widely used in production for model routing and provider switching without code changes.
tools.pricing_paid: Self-hosted free; LiteLLM Proxy Enterprise from ~$499/month for advanced features

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching library specifically designed for LLM APIs. Supports multiple embedding models for similarity search, pluggable vector stores (FAISS, Redis, Milvus), and multiple eviction policies. Integrates with LangChain and directly with OpenAI clients.

tools.name: Redis Semantic Cache
tools.description: Redis Stack's vector similarity search enables semantic caching for LLM responses at low latency. Stores query embeddings and responses; returns cached results for semantically similar future queries. Redis Cloud managed offering simplifies production deployment.
tools.pricing_paid: Redis Cloud from $0 (30MB free tier) to custom enterprise pricing; self-hosted is free

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and optimization platform that sits as a proxy in front of LLM APIs. Provides cost tracking per request, prompt caching analytics, semantic caching, rate limiting, and detailed usage dashboards. One-line integration for OpenAI and Anthropic.
tools.pricing_paid: Free up to 10,000 requests/month; Pro at $20/month; Team/Enterprise custom pricing

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: Popular LLM application framework with built-in caching integrations (InMemoryCache, RedisCache, SQLiteCache, GPTCache), prompt template management, and chain optimization utilities. Widely used to add semantic caching and prompt management to existing LLM applications.
tools.pricing_paid: LangSmith observability platform from $39/month; LangChain library is open-source free

tools.name: Bifrost
tools.description: LLM gateway that combines semantic caching with provider-native prompt caching for best-in-class cost reduction. Pairs both caching layers in a single proxy, plus routing and fallbacks. Highlighted in 2026 production configurations for achieving maximum cache coverage.
tools.pricing_paid: Contact for pricing; usage-based enterprise model

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.description: Unified API router providing access to dozens of LLM providers with automatic model routing, cost comparison, and fallback handling. Useful for right-sizing model selection by routing tasks to the cheapest provider passing quality thresholds without managing multiple API keys.
tools.pricing_paid: Pay-as-you-go at provider cost plus small markup (~$0 platform fee for standard usage); no monthly subscription

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway and observability platform offering semantic caching, multi-provider load balancing, automatic retries, and detailed cost analytics. Supports 200+ models and provides a virtual key system for secure API key management across teams.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier available; Growth plan from $49/month; Enterprise custom

tools.name: vLLM
tools.description: High-throughput open-source inference server for self-hosted LLMs. Uses PagedAttention for efficient KV cache management, continuous batching to maximize GPU utilization, and quantization support. Ideal for teams running open-weight models (Llama, Qwen, Gemma, DeepSeek) to eliminate per-token API costs entirely.

tools.name: Prem AI
tools.description: All-in-one LLM optimization platform covering prompt compression, semantic caching, model routing, and output constraints. Their documented case study achieved 80% API cost reduction in 6 weeks using a combined strategy of all four techniques.
tools.pricing_paid: Starter and Pro tiers available; contact for enterprise pricing

quick_wins: Enable provider-native prompt caching immediately by moving your static system prompt and any fixed context to the top of your prompt unchanged — this takes under an hour to implement and can cut input token costs by up to 90% on repeated calls with zero quality trade-off.

Set explicit max_tokens limits on all API calls and switch verbose free-text responses to structured JSON schemas — output tokens cost 4–5x more than input tokens, and this single change commonly reduces output token usage by 30–50% with no engineering effort beyond prompt edits.

Audit your current model usage and move classification, extraction, and simple FAQ tasks to a budget-tier model (GPT-3.5, Claude Haiku 4.5 at $1/$5, or Gemini Flash) — most teams find 60–70% of their requests don't need a frontier model, delivering immediate per-call savings.

Add a semantic cache (Redis, GPTCache, or Helicone's built-in cache) in front of your highest-volume, most repetitive query endpoint — a 45% cache hit rate on a 1M-query-per-month workload eliminates nearly half your API spend on that route with a one-time integration.

Switch any non-real-time batch workloads (nightly data enrichment, content generation pipelines, offline labeling) to the provider's batch API — Anthropic and OpenAI both offer 50% discounts on batch jobs, requiring only a trivial code change to the API call method.
